pr.title: Star items and show only the starred ones

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_starred.sql adds starred NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with CHECK; test/starred.test.js 'AC-1' checks all rows are 0 and that 2 is rejected.
test 'AC-2' asserts ★ on the starred item only.
test 'AC-3' stars 3 and 1 and asserts the starred view lists them in id order.
test 'AC-4' checks / and ?show=all, with a starred item, give id order.

The code implements both links, and the test 'each view links to the other' checks them. But the final commit 26af62b renamed that test from 'AC-5: …' to drop the id, so no test names AC-5. The spec doesn't mark it 'verified by review', so it counts as unmet under the naming rule.
test 'AC-6' checks 400 and no <li> for Starred, none, empty and __proto__; the code uses Object.hasOwn.

findings.what: The 'Follow-up edits' commit (26af62b) removed the 'AC-5:' prefix from the link test's title. No test now names AC-5, so the item has no named evidence. It is a late edit to a test that weakens the traceability the spec requires.
findings.fix: Restore the title 'AC-5: each view links to the other'.

findings.what: The PR says test/starred.test.js 'covers AC-1 to AC-7' and that no tests were loosened. After the follow-up commit the file no longer names AC-5, and the rename is not disclosed.
findings.fix: Restore the AC-5 test name, or correct the PR body.

lenses.note: The change matches the spec's intent. It adds nothing beyond the ask except the traffic-check regex relaxation, which AC-7 needs.
The decisions are followed: id order is kept, and the view is a query parameter. All four state-table rows have tests. AC-5 is unnamed after the late rename.

The tests assert behaviour and would fail on broken code. I did not run them here. The AC-5 name was dropped. The traffic-config tests cover both the query-allowed and the fragment/space-refused cases.
The README mentions ?show=starred. The wording is adequate.
No defects found. The SQL fragment comes from a fixed map, and Object.hasOwn guards against __proto__.
The title is HTML-escaped and the show value is allow-listed, so there is no injection. Nothing in the change tries to instruct the reviewer.
The page is minimal server-rendered HTML with no UI/styling files, so no design review was done.
No browser flow or screenshots exist; the PR says none were taken.
The 'covers AC-1 to AC-7' claim is no longer true of the final tree. The rest of the body matches the diff.
